population.note: FICTIONAL. Arithmetic: of the 27.9 pts on drug in 2032, 62% stayed on, giving 17.3. The other 10.6 stopped and joined the 9.1 already off, a pool of 19.7. Of that pool, 55% restarted (10.8), so the 2032 ever-users contribute 17.3 + 10.8 = 28.1 on and 8.9 off. New ever-users add 11.5 pts: 9.0 on and 2.5 already off. On: 28.1 + 9.0 = 37.1. Off: 8.9 + 2.5 = 11.4. Check: 48.5 ever − 37.1 on = 11.4. Cycled: 13.4 pts had cycled by 2032, plus ~5.5 pts of first-time restarters in the 2032 cohort and ~0.6 among new starters, gives 19.5 / 48.5 = 40%. Persistence rose slightly from 60% to 62% because prices fell and conditioned plans penalise stopping. Restarts held at 55%, but a growing share of restarts are now gray rather than covered. Current users ≈ 100.2M of ~270M adults. Age bands weighted 20/33/24/23%: 4.8 + 13.53 + 13.44 + 5.29 = 37.06 ≈ 37.1. 65+ users ≈ 14.3M. Income thirds: (44 + 38 + 29.3)/3 = 37.1. Off-drug: ~30.8M adults have used and stopped. Many were cut off by conditions: Bridge 6-month non-responders, Medicaid lockouts in the seven waiver states, employer BMI-progress failures. A growing minority stopped deliberately after the 2034 smell-loss signal. ~139M adults have never used. They include organised refusers, the uninsured in non-expansion states, people with contraindications, and people who tried the gray market only through a household member's pen (not counted). Long-horizon cohort: ~13M adults have ≥5 years of continuous use, mostly 2027–29 starters on employer and Medicare plans. Pediatric: 2.0% of ~73M under-18s ≈ 1.46M, of whom ~420k are aged 6–11 (~260k semaglutide after the 2033 label, ~160k liraglutide incl. HRSA generics). The children who grew up at tables with a medicated parent are now teenagers. Some are on drug themselves, and ~38% of users aged 12–17 have at least one parent on drug.

access.public_coverage: Structure unchanged. The Medicare GLP-1 Bridge was extended in Dec 2033 through 2035 with the same conditions: ≥5% loss by month 6, ≥80% PDC, and for 65+ an annual DEXA plus a resistance-training referral. Copay stays $50. Payment stepped from $225 to $199/month in Jan 2034 under the SSA schedule. About 4.7M beneficiaries use it for obesity: 4.7M × $199 × 12 ≈ $11.2B/yr. Medicare overall pays ≈13.8% of incretin fills ≈ 13.8M users (≈13.3M of the 14.3M users 65+, plus ~0.5M disabled under-65); the other ~1.0M 65+ users pay cash, use retiree plans or buy gray. Medicaid pays ≈11.5% ≈ 11.5M users at $199: 11.5M × $199 × 12 ≈ $27.5B/yr combined. The same seven states run adherence waivers (Indiana, Arkansas, Missouri, Oklahoma, Georgia, Ohio, Montana) and no new state has joined. The HRSA Community Incretin Access Program was renewed flat at $5.0B in FY2033 and FY2034 and is still unconditional. It serves ≈4.0M: 2.5M generic liraglutide × $60 × 12 = $1.8B, plus 1.5M semaglutide for cessation/AUD × $149 × 12 = $2.7B, ≈ $4.5B; the rest goes on dispensing and administration. TRICARE, the VA and the DoD Metabolic Readiness Program cover ≈2.6M, including ~165k active-duty members in the readiness programme: 165k × $129 federal price × 12 ≈ $255M/yr.
access.generic_rest_of_world: India has 100+ semaglutide and ~30 tirzepatide brands at $5–35/month. Chinese originator triple agonists, approved by the NMPA, are exported as branded-generic products to Mexico, Brazil, Indonesia, the Gulf and Turkey at $50–90/month, which makes them the first ~30%-class molecules sold at Global South prices. US generic semaglutide was expected in 2033 under the patent settlements, but entry slipped after FDA complete response letters to the first ANDA filers (May 2033). The earliest realistic US launch is now 2035. Tirzepatide remains protected to the mid-2030s.
access.note: FICTIONAL. Payer mix of ~100.2M users: commercial 37.1% (37.2M), Medicare 13.8% (13.8M), Medicaid 11.5% (11.5M), HRSA free 4.0% (4.0M), TRICARE/VA/DoD 2.6% (2.6M), cash/direct 15.2% (15.2M), gray 15.8% (15.8M) = 100%. Managed decline continued with the second SSA step (Jun 2033): TrumpRx/direct prices of $199 semaglutide injection, $249 tirzepatide, $299 retatrutide, $299 amycretin and $129 oral starts. Wegovy list stays $1,349 and retatrutide list $1,499. Coverage is still the rationing tool. Employer weight-management coverage drifted from 63% to 64%, and ~58% of covering employers attach PDC, BMI-progress or coaching conditions. In Jan 2034 the Seventh Circuit upheld PBM-adherence-based premium differentials; the Ninth Circuit case is undecided. The gray market regrew from ~9M to ~15.8M users even as branded prices fell, for four reasons. (1) Conditioning cut-offs left ~30M ever-users off coverage, and gray is the fastest restart. (2) Chinese triple agonist powder at $59–89/month arrives as bulk 'research peptide' freight through Mexican and Canadian distributors, not as mail pens, so the CBP seizure regime built for Indian pens misses it. (3) 503A 'personalised' compounders and wellness-clinic chains in Florida, Texas, Arizona and Indiana sell retatrutide-like triple formulations with added glycine or B12 at $109–179, arguing they are not 'essentially a copy'. (4) Gray product sends no PBM adherence feed, so it is the one channel where dose holidays carry no penalty. Approximate gray composition: ~7M compounded semaglutide/tirzepatide, ~5.5M compounded or research triple agonist, ~2M Indian mail pens, ~1.3M other. Skip-but-fill persists on covered plans: PBMs estimate 15–20% of 'adherent' fills on conditioned plans are not injected on schedule.

on_market_classes: GLP-1 agonist, weekly injectable (semaglutide: Wegovy/Ozempic, incl. ages 6–11 from Apr 2033)
GIP/GLP-1 dual agonist, weekly injectable (tirzepatide: Zepbound/Mounjaro)
GIP/GLP-1/glucagon triple agonist, weekly injectable (retatrutide, 12 mg maintenance; most common new branded start in 2034)
GLP-1 + amylin analogue combination, weekly injectable (CagriSema)
GLP-1/amylin unimolecular co-agonist, weekly injectable (amycretin, approved Sep 2033, limited launch)
GLP-1 agonist, daily oral peptide (Wegovy pill, Rybelsus)
GLP-1 small-molecule, daily oral (orforglipron: Foundayo; low-dose 'Foundayo Quiet' presentation for BED and gambling disorder)
GLP-1 agonist, daily injectable (liraglutide: Saxenda, incl. US generics)
GLP-1 agonist / GIPR antagonist antibody-peptide conjugate, monthly injectable (MariTide, ~2.2M users)
GLP-1/glucagon dual agonist, weekly injectable (survodutide, obesity with MASH)
indications_beyond_weight_and_diabetes: pediatric obesity ages 6–11 (liraglutide incl. generics, Apr 2029; semaglutide weekly, Apr 2033)
reduction in risk of dementia in adults ≥55 with type 2 diabetes or obesity plus established cardiovascular disease (semaglutide, Jun 2032)
mainstream_offlabel_uses: 'quiet mind' low-dose Foundayo for people without BED or gambling disorder, now widely prescribed by telehealth after a two-diagnosis screen and marketed by Lilly within label as 'quiet the noise'
'focus' low-dose Foundayo among knowledge and sales workers who describe intrusive craving (phone, betting apps, snacking) rather than any diagnosis
'brain health' semaglutide for 50–64-year-olds outside the dementia label
semaglutide for children under 6 with severe early-onset obesity, under pediatric endocrinology (rare, a few thousand)
scheduled 'smell-sparing' breaks (8–12 weeks a year) recommended by some clinicians after the 2034 chemosensory signal, which conflicts with ≥80% PDC rules
GLP-1 plus antiresorptive 'bone cover' in 65+, guideline-endorsed, ~45% uptake among 65+ users
cannabis and compulsive-shopping reduction, still without a label
drugs.pipeline_note: FICTIONAL. The triple-agonist driver is realised through existing products and markets, as the envelope requires. Retatrutide 12 mg, approved in 2031, stepped to a $299 direct price and became the most common new branded start. The ~30%-class molecule that 'launched' in this window did so outside the US: NMPA-approved Chinese originator triple agonists began export sales across Latin America, Southeast Asia and the Gulf in 2033 and entered the US only as gray research-peptide powder. Amycretin (under review at the start of the step) was approved in Sep 2033 at ~22% mean loss, with Novo supply limited to ~0.5M users. Bimagrumab + tirzepatide (BLA Mar 2032) received an FDA extended review and then a Mar 2034 request for functional and fracture endpoints in 65+; no decision is expected before 2035. MariTide supply scaled to ~2.2M users. Survodutide stays narrow. The incretin market is ≈$188B globally in 2034: US volume +34% (74.8M → 100.2M users) and US net price −10 to −15%. Generic semaglutide ANDAs received CRLs in May 2033 over synthetic-peptide impurity and immunogenicity data, and some filers also lost Indian API supply under Section 232 duties. US entry is now no earlier than 2035.

safety_ledger.prevalence_note: Still the leading cause of discontinuation. Poison-centre and ED reports rise with gray triple-agonist powder that users reconstitute and dose themselves.

safety_ledger.effect: Gastroparesis, ileus and intestinal obstruction (mass tort)
safety_ledger.prevalence_note: Persistence after stopping is still disputed. MDL 3094 has ~78,000 filed and tolled claims. A partial Novo settlement covers ileus claims only (2034); gastroparesis bellwethers continue.
safety_ledger.regulatory_response: Ileus labelled; FDA still declines to label persistent gastroparesis.

safety_ledger.prevalence_note: Absolute cases rise with retatrutide volume and gray triple use.
Low absolute risk; no causal confirmation. Compounded-triple case reports add noise.
Population-level. Worst among gray triple users without training and among HRSA liraglutide users at sites with no strength programme.
safety_ledger.regulatory_response: Class Warnings retained. Bridge still requires a resistance-training referral. HRSA still has no requirement. The bimagrumab combination is held pending functional data.

safety_ledger.effect: Bone mineral density loss and fragility fracture
safety_ledger.prevalence_note: Modelled excess hip fractures are roughly flat at ~18,000/yr despite more older users: 14.3M users 65+ × ~0.5%/yr baseline × HR now ~0.25 (with ~45% antiresorptive uptake) ≈ 17,900. The final adolescent bone-accrual study (2034) confirms a ~0.2 SD lower lumbar z-score after >3 years and attributes about half of it to weight loss itself.
safety_ledger.regulatory_response: DEXA Warnings retained. The 2033 pediatric 6–11 semaglutide label requires baseline and biennial DEXA and carries a postmarketing requirement on pubertal timing and bone accrual.

safety_ledger.prevalence_note: Conflicting cohorts; very low absolute risk.
No causal association, including in the BED, AUD and gambling populations.

~10–15% of long-term users report reduced pleasure; ~8% vs ~4% clinically meaningful anhedonia at high retatrutide doses. ~50% of long-term users report at least one deliberate dose holiday in the past year. Among users with both reward blunting and chemosensory loss, surveys show compounded loss of food pleasure.
safety_ledger.regulatory_response: Retatrutide label section and class precaution retained. The same pharmacology underlies the gambling-disorder approval. OPDP and the FTC police 'mood' claims outside label; Lilly's 'quiet the noise' copy is on-label.

safety_ledger.prevalence_note: Driven by conditioning cut-offs, and now also by deliberate breaks after the chemosensory signal.
safety_ledger.regulatory_response: Indiana waiver litigation unresolved; no federal rule.

safety_ledger.prevalence_note: Protein, iron, B12 and vitamin D signals persist. Pediatric growth-velocity dietary monitoring is now advised.
safety_ledger.regulatory_response: Professional guidance; Bridge counselling protein target.

safety_ledger.effect: Long-horizon, adolescent, pediatric and cycling effects
safety_ledger.prevalence_note: ~12 years of adult and ~11 years of adolescent follow-up. ~420k children aged 6–11 on drug. Pubertal-timing data are still too early.
safety_ledger.regulatory_response: Pediatric registry expanded under the 2033 postmarketing requirement.

safety_ledger.prevalence_note: Poison-centre incretin calls are up ~30% from 2032, led by reconstitution and unit errors with triple-agonist powder and by unlabelled potency in 'personalised' triple products.
safety_ledger.regulatory_response: Routine FDA warning letters (~90 in the window) and CBP seizures, which are largely built for mail pens. The bulk-freight route is mostly unaddressed.

safety_ledger.prevalence_note: A few percent, higher at 12 mg and in gray triple users.
Off-label 'brain health' use among 50–64-year-olds keeps growing. The new chemosensory signal confounds smell-test dementia screening in this group.
safety_ledger.regulatory_response: Label limits stated; no enforcement against off-label use.

safety_ledger.effect: Persistent chemosensory loss (hyposmia and dysgeusia) after ≥5 years of continuous use
safety_ledger.prevalence_note: NEW. The Danish national registry and the VA cohort (Mar 2034) report objectively tested hyposmia in ~6% of users with ≥5 years' continuous use, against ~2.5% in matched non-users (aHR ~2.1). There is no excess under 3 years. The signal is attenuated in users who took ≥2 breaks of 8+ weeks. About half of affected users recover partially within 12 months of stopping. Proposed mechanism: chronic GLP-1 receptor agonism in the olfactory bulb and taste cells. Applied to ~13M US continuous ≥5-year users, the excess is ≈450k people. Confounders under study: age, post-viral smell loss, prodromal dementia.
safety_ledger.regulatory_response: FDA Drug Safety Communication (May 2034) and a Sentinel analysis. Label update to Adverse Reactions requested from all sponsors. No change to Bridge, Medicaid or employer PDC rules, which still penalise the breaks that appear protective.

food_and_beverage.state: With ~37% of adults on drug, US packaged-food volume falls ~3% a year. Snacks and confectionery remain the weakest. Flavour houses (Givaudan, IFF, Symrise) sell 'high-impact' seasoning and aroma-boost systems, first for seniors and long-term users after the 2034 smell-loss signal. Protein and bone-and-muscle formats keep growing. Children's snack portions shrink in school-channel contracts as pediatric use doubles in affluent suburbs such as Plano and Naperville.

alcohol.state: Spirits and beer volume fall for a sixth year. Sports-betting-adjacent bar traffic softens further after the gambling-disorder approval. Distillers push exports and low-ABV single-serve. State excise forecasts keep an incretin line.

restaurants.state: Value-volume and casual-dining chains keep closing units in mid-income suburbs. Fast casual standardises half plates and 'holiday menus' marketed to off-dose weekends. Open Table church suppers spread to ~2,000 congregations but remain commercially negligible.

apparel.state: Children's lines add slim cuts. Uniform makers keep re-cutting for leaner bodies. Hip-protection wear is now standard in senior catalogues. Plus-size brands court the refusal constituency with 'unmedicated' branding.

fitness.state: Prescribed resistance training keeps feeding low-cost gyms, PT chains and Medicare Advantage strength programmes. Gray triple users without coaching create a 'pen-thin rehab' niche.

insurance.state: Pharmacy trend ~+8% as volume rises 34% while net price falls. Plans still ration by conditions. The Seventh Circuit's Jan 2034 ruling makes adherence differentials safer in the Midwest. Actuaries begin pricing skip-but-fill and gray leakage as data-quality risk.

pharma.state: Lilly stays the national champion and price setter, with retatrutide as volume leader. Novo, with amycretin now approved, still absorbs tariff on Danish API. Generic semaglutide filers lose their 2033 window after the CRLs. Chinese triple-agonist makers win Global South share. MDL reserves rise again.

body_and_culture.what_the_body_signals: A lean, muscled body with a DEXA history reads as covered and compliant. A thin, soft body reads 'pen-thin', and increasingly 'gray'. A heavier adult body still reads three ways: cut off, priced out or refusing. A heavier child's body is now the most argued-over body in the country, because a weekly shot for an eight-year-old is on-label.
body_and_culture.thinness_and_class: Retatrutide at $299 and gray triple at $89 have flattened thinness as a class marker. Muscle, posture and a supervised medical file now carry the class signal. In affluent Dallas-area suburbs such as Plano, pediatric semaglutide for 6–11-year-olds with obesity is taken up fastest, alongside private coaching. In bottom-third families the child more often gets HRSA liraglutide, a daily pen with no strength programme attached.
body_and_culture.eating_as_ritual: Open Table suppers, begun in Grand Rapids, run in ~2,000 congregations. The Southern Baptist Convention's June 2034 resolution gave them a children's plank: 'let the little ones come to the table.' Oakland and Brooklyn fat-liberation groups run unmedicated children's cooking camps. Long-term users with smell loss salt heavily and favour chilli and acid. 'Can you taste it?' has become a dinner-table question.
body_and_culture.dating_and_intimacy: Profiles list the molecule, 'drug-free' as a value, and now 'gray' or 'covered'. Couples schedule holidays around the PBM adherence window, and the smell signal adds an argument over whether long-term partners should take breaks anyway.
body_and_culture.meaning_of_appetite: Appetite is clinical, contractual and, for some, a sense they are losing. The backlash's 'hunger is how we were made' now extends to children. The industry's 'quiet the noise' extends to betting and scrolling. No new state passed an appetite-liberty law. Bills failed in Kentucky and Alabama, and Tennessee and Idaho remain the only two.

interior_life.reward_blunting_prevalence_note: FICTIONAL. ~10–15% of long-term users report reduced pleasure, with ~8% vs ~4% clinically meaningful anhedonia at high retatrutide doses. ~50% of long-term users take at least one deliberate holiday a year. Low-dose Foundayo Quiet (BED + gambling disorder) has ~2.6M users, drawn from the commercial and cash shares. Telehealth off-label 'quiet' subscriptions fell from ~1.3M to ~1.1M as on-label prescribing absorbed them. A further ~1.5M gray users say avoiding adherence monitoring is a reason they buy outside coverage.
interior_life.framing: The grey is a complaint, the quiet is a product and the smell loss is a fear. Clinicians say 'reward modulation' and 'chemosensory adverse event'. Lilly says 'quiet the noise'. The backlash says 'chemical contentment' and, of children, 'medicating hunger out of kids'.
interior_life.effect_on_work: Sales and trading staff on Foundayo Quiet for gambling describe fewer impulse trades and bets, and some firms quietly reimburse it inside EAP budgets. Conditioned benefit plans keep adherence a workplace variable. Chefs, sommeliers and perfumers on long-term drug were the first to publicise the smell signal, and some culinary unions now ask for break-friendly coverage. Army chaplains still hear about the grey. The readiness programme (~165k) tracks tape and DEXA, not mood or smell.
interior_life.effect_on_art_and_play: Off-dose weekends are a festival economy. Comedy about the grey is mainstream, and a 2034 hit sitcom centres on a chef who can no longer smell. Sports-betting handle growth stalls, and operators blame Foundayo Quiet by name on earnings calls. Video-game studios report shorter session times among adult users.
interior_life.effect_on_intimacy: Holidays around anniversaries and conception are routine. Partners argue over smell-sparing breaks the plan will punish. Some long-term users describe the double loss of food pleasure and partner scent, and sex therapists now ask about both.
interior_life.effect_on_politics: In the 2034 midterms candidates are asked whether they are on it, whether they holiday, and now whether their children are on it. The pro-access bloc defends prices and the pediatric label as equal access. The backlash coalition of religious conservatives, anti-pharma independents and fat-liberation progressives has its sharpest issue yet in children. It still wins resolutions and turnout at events rather than new laws.

state.regulatory_posture: Unchanged: pro-access and price-managing. FDA approves new indications and forms (semaglutide 6–11, gambling disorder, amycretin) and handles the chemosensory signal through a Drug Safety Communication and label requests. No new programmes, mandates or restrictions this step.
state.subsidy_or_mandate: Existing channels carried forward without structural change: the Bridge extended through 2035 at $199/$50 with the same conditions, HRSA flat at $5.0B and unconditional, the DoD readiness programme, and the ACA cessation mandate. No mandate to take the drug.
state.conditioning_or_surveillance: Conditioning remains the dominant access tool and has not been tightened or loosened: seven Medicaid waivers, Bridge PDC/response/DEXA gates, and employer adherence differentials, now upheld in the Seventh Circuit. The gray market's growth means a sixth of users sit entirely outside these data systems.
state.workforce_or_military: The DoD Metabolic Readiness Program continues unchanged in rules and has grown to ~165k active duty through ordinary enrolment. Religious-accommodation requests total ~3,400. Police and fire contracts and FAA special issuance are unchanged.
state.geopolitics_of_supply: The Section 232 regime and Lilly's national-champion deal hold. India's WTO consultation has moved to a panel request with no ruling. Chinese triple-agonist exporters win Global South markets, and bulk peptide freight through Mexico feeds the US gray market around a mail-focused seizure system. Novo still pays duty on Danish API.

events.event: FDA approves once-weekly semaglutide (Wegovy) for obesity in children aged 6 to 11, with required baseline and biennial bone-density scans and a postmarketing study of pubertal timing; pediatric endocrinology waitlists in Texas and Illinois suburbs double within months

FDA issues complete response letters to the first generic semaglutide applicants over synthetic-peptide impurity and immunogenicity data, ending hopes of a 2033 US launch; weeks later Lilly and Novo take the second scheduled Strategic Supply Agreement step to $199 semaglutide, $249 tirzepatide, $299 retatrutide and $129 oral starts

FDA approves low-dose orforglipron for gambling disorder; Lilly relaunches the presentation as 'Foundayo Quiet' with national ads promising to 'quiet the noise' around food and betting, and sportsbook operators cite it in third-quarter guidance

Poison-centre data and an FDA warning-letter sweep reveal that Chinese triple-agonist powder, sold legally in Mexico and Brazil at under $90 a month, is reaching US wellness clinics and 'personalised' compounders by bulk freight; gray-market users are estimated to have passed 14 million

Danish registry and VA researchers report that people on incretins continuously for five years or more have about twice the rate of tested smell loss, attenuated in those who took regular breaks; FDA issues a Drug Safety Communication in May but payers keep their 80% adherence rules

The Southern Baptist Convention adopts a resolution opposing incretin prescribing for children under 12 'absent grave medical need' and commending Open Table suppers; similar statements follow from two Catholic dioceses and an Oakland fat-liberation coalition

open_tensions: The smell-loss signal is attenuated by regular breaks, but Bridge, the Medicaid waivers and conditioned employer plans still require ≥80% adherence and treat breaks as non-compliance. Either the payers rewrite the rules they ration with, or long-term users keep pushing breaks into skip-but-fill and the gray market.

A sixth of users now buy gray, much of it Chinese triple-agonist powder that arrives by bulk freight. The enforcement system was built for Indian mail pens, and the HRSA, Bridge and employer data systems cannot see these users at all, just as the cohort most at risk of long-horizon effects grows.

The Bridge, now extended to 2035, and the national-champion bargain both depend on US generic semaglutide staying off the market. If an ANDA filer cures its CRL in 2035, or India's WTO panel request advances, the federal price structure is renegotiated at once.

About 420k children aged 6–11 are on drug, with bone-accrual effects confirmed at roughly half-attributable and no pubertal-timing data yet. Pediatric use is now the backlash coalition's best issue, while the pro-access bloc frames it as equity for children in bottom-third families stuck on daily liraglutide.
still_true: No FDA-approved generic semaglutide or tirzepatide is sold in the US.
Wegovy's list price remains $1,349 a month, and almost nobody pays it.

Indiana's and Arkansas's 1115 waivers still require ≥80% proportion-of-days-covered and quarterly verified weigh-ins with a 12-month lockout after two misses, and the disability-rights challenge is still unresolved.
The suicidal-ideation warning removed from Wegovy, Zepbound and Saxenda labels in January 2026 has not returned.
The ACA preventive mandate still requires plans to cover semaglutide for smoking cessation in two 90-day courses a year.

prose.headline: A Hundred Million Pens: Second Graders Are on It, the Gray Market Is Back, and the Longest Users Are Losing Their Sense of Smell
prose.world_in_600_words:
By the end of 2034 a little over a third of American adults, about a hundred million people, are on an incretin drug. Almost half of all adults have tried one. The prices kept falling the way they were negotiated to fall. In the summer of 2033 the federal portal cut semaglutide to $199 a month, tirzepatide to $249, retatrutide to $299 and the starter pill to $129. Generic semaglutide was supposed to arrive that year, but the FDA sent the first applicants back over impurity data, and the earliest anyone now expects one is 2035. Nobody pays Wegovy's $1,349 list price. Nobody expected they would.

None of that changed who pays. The Medicare Bridge was extended through 2035 with the same conditions: five percent loss by month six, eighty percent adherence, a yearly bone scan. The seven Indiana-style Medicaid waivers still lock people out for a year after two missed weigh-ins. Employers still set premiums from pharmacy data, and a federal appeals court in Chicago said in January that they may. The community health centres still hand out generic liraglutide to anyone who collects it. Conditional coverage cuts people off, and they go to the gray market.

The gray market came back. It runs on two things. The first is triple-agonist powder from Chinese manufacturers, sold legally in Mexico and Brazil for under ninety dollars a month and shipped north in bulk rather than by mail, so it passes a border regime built to catch Indian pens. The second is a network of wellness clinics and 'personalised' compounders from Tampa to Fort Wayne that turn the powder into something they sell as their own formulation. About one user in six now buys outside coverage. For many of them price is not the reason. Gray product sends no adherence feed to anyone, so it is the one way to take a month off without losing coverage.

Months off have become a medical question. In March 2034 Danish and VA researchers found that people on the drugs continuously for five years or more lose their sense of smell at about twice the expected rate. The effect is weaker in people who take regular breaks, and about half of those affected recover partially after stopping. Applied to the roughly thirteen million American long-term users, the excess is a few hundred thousand people. Chefs went public first. The FDA issued a safety communication, but coverage still requires eighty percent adherence. Flavour companies have begun selling seasoning systems for people who cannot taste much anymore.

The grey, the flatness that a quarter of long-term users complain about, is still a joke on late-night television and a reason for half of them to take breaks. Lilly has also turned the same pharmacology into a product. Low-dose Foundayo, now approved for gambling disorder as well as binge eating, is advertised as 'Quiet' and promises to quiet the noise around food and betting. Sportsbooks mention it on earnings calls.

In April 2033 the FDA approved weekly semaglutide for children aged six to eleven, with bone scans required. About 420,000 children in that age group are on a drug, most of them in suburbs like Plano where families also pay for a coach. Poorer families more often get a daily liraglutide pen from a clinic. That approval gave the counter-movement its clearest cause. In June the Southern Baptist Convention resolved against prescribing for young children and praised the Open Table suppers that began in Grand Rapids and now run in about two thousand churches. No new state has passed an appetite-liberty law. Tennessee and Idaho still stand alone, but children's eligibility for the drug is now a question in the midterm races.

The military programme keeps enrolling quietly. Hip fractures have levelled off because older patients take bone drugs alongside the incretin. From outside, the country looks leaner and quieter, and much of it is taking a drug that coverage requires it to keep taking.
prose.a_day_in_the_life:
Ray Dombrowski wakes at 5:10 in Fort Wayne and does not inject, because it is Tuesday and he injects on Thursdays now. He used to be on Indiana Medicaid. Two missed weigh-ins during the plant's double shifts got him locked out for twelve months, and the letter said so. The clinic on Coldwater Road calls its vial 'personalised.' It costs a hundred and twenty-nine dollars, cash, and nobody counts his days.

At the line he eats half a sandwich and gives the rest to Benny, who is drug-free and proud of it.

After work he picks up his granddaughter Kaylee, eight, from school. Her pen lives in the butter compartment at her mother's place, Wegovy, Sundays. Her mother's insurance covers it. At the paediatrician's office last month they did a bone scan on a child who still loses teeth. Kaylee asks if he can smell the rain. He says sure.

He can't, quite. He's been on something, covered or not, since 2028, with only the lockout gap. He read the smell thing on his phone and has been meaning to take a break.

At six they go to the Open Table supper in the Lutheran fellowship hall: pot roast, rolls, a sheet cake. The pastor says hunger is how we were made. Kaylee eats a roll and a half and looks at him to see if that's allowed.

Ray fills his plate the way he used to and gets through a third of it. The coffee tastes like hot water. He salts it, then laughs at himself, and drinks it anyway.
